book_question: What is the Grace, really? (Book II; Darrow fights on his feet but cannot run: every fight held, not chased)

chapter.question: Will the Lowmarch hide a captain who will not kneel, and what will it cost the carter who brings him home?

slots.plan: The first miles of the Holloway below the winch-house, at a walk: Wren off the mountain for the first time and counting everything; Hollis at war with the mule; Maelis's count on the knee; Ash ranging ahead and reporting nothing. Rae tells him she told the mare her name, as she said she would (c04.1a). Then the banner that is not grey, coming up the Holloway toward Coldmere: Darrow wants to go and see whose it is, sure it is Aldric's; Rae will not drive her cart into a Knight-Confessor's column and turns off the Holloway onto the drove road round the far side of the tarn; Hollis backs her; they have it out on the road, out loud. Camp at a sheepfold; Wren's first night under a whole sky.
slots.turn: Darrow, who once rode sixty men into a river because he was sure, tries to take the road toward the banner and ends by giving it to a carter who is right; Rae, who has never asked anyone's leave on the Holloway, finds she wanted his.

slots.plan: A drove-road hamlet with its door barred and a fresh writ on its bell-post: the Captain of the Ninth's name above every other (c04.14a), and under it, new, the Mender Vorne (T8 plant, thread 8). The reeve will not sell bread to anything off Rae's cart: a carter's custom spent on the man she carries, the first time it has cost her. Maelis reads her own name on a writ and says plainly what she makes of it. At dusk a Faithless man of the hamlet, who has heard of the captain who stood up at the gate and would not kneel, leaves bread at the fold (c01.5b: the Faithless take heart).
slots.turn: The Lowmarch reads his name before it sees his face, and Maelis's under it; Rae learns what carrying him costs a carter on her own road, and keeps carrying.

micro.ask: The reeve asks, through the bars, who rides on the Thorne cart. What does Darrow say?
options: "Darrow of Edgemoor. The one on your post."
"Salt, a sick man and his nurse. Ask the carter."
Let Rae answer for her own cart.

slots.plan: Noon in a turnip field below the drove road: a Hollowed knight in a Lance's surcoat walks east through the rows, slow and straight, past the company as if they were posts (T4: the Hollowing is on this side of the Wend; thread 4). Darrow tries to stop him, to turn him, to get a name, and cannot. Wren knows how to make a Hollowed man take water, does it without being asked, and goes white doing it. Rae tells her grandmother's story of the grey country east of the Wend, where they walk home: told to frighten a child, never believed, until this noon. They let him go east.
slots.turn: Darrow, who called the far cots sick men, watches one walk with somewhere to go; the company stops being a party in flight and becomes one with a question.

slots.plan: A carter on the drove road brings the news: the banner turned back at the Coldmere crossroads on a rider from Calden and went south, the Calden way (book2.question). Into Coldmere at dusk: the inn on the tarn, the bell-house across the road where the list was read; Rae at home (the taproom calls her by name, the old ones by her grandmother's; the village has heard of the bell); her uncle at the tap, his welcome and his book. Then the dealer's yard on the fair-ground: Thistle, lame in the off fore, alive, eating a stranger's hay on Darrow's word; the dealer lets slip that the carter has paid the mare's keep since the fair; asked why, Rae answers plainly.
slots.turn: Darrow learns what Rae has done for him without a word said, and she learns he will not let it go unsaid; the mare is still the dealer's until the debt is stood.

slots.plan: The levy sergeant and six men come through Coldmere looking for Faithless and a woman Mender. Darrow and Hollis go up into the loft over the inn's byre with Ash, where Hollis cannot whisper; Maelis goes into the kitchen as a cook and is a terrible one; Wren keeps the sergeant's questions in her ledger from behind the tap; Rae talks oxen with him in the yard for an hour, until he leaves knowing nothing and with an opinion on yokes (rae.road, any tier). On his way out the sergeant asks the uncle about the Mender Vorne; the uncle has never heard of her, and looks at Rae.
slots.turn: Rae holds a whole village's danger with an hour of talk while the fastest blade of the Lowmarch hides in hay; the uncle's look tells Darrow the inn's silence has a price, and whose book it will be written in.

slots.plan: Dice night in the taproom. At the next table a Grace-burned knight of another Lance drinks and wins, a man who kneels at every field-stone on the road (q2.inn folded into the beat: the Book II temptation, `plan temptation add` when written). In the yard a cart's axle goes and he lifts the cart off a carter's boy with his hands, and his hands are frosted when he sets it down. He knows the Faithless captain by the stick and the face and offers him the fast road with a full heart: down to the crossroads stone in the morning, kneel, and be what you were. Warden's Eye shows the frost going in.
slots.turn: Darrow meets the man he would be on the fast road and likes him, and the temptation is real because it works.

micro.ask: The knight asks Darrow to kneel beside him at the crossroads stone in the morning. What does Darrow do?
options: Tell him plainly what he saw painted under the House: a kneeling knight, and the light going up out of him.
Buy him a drink and say nothing.

slots.plan: Hollis and Darrow walk to the crossroads to read the column's tracks: the banner's riders turned back south for Calden; one horse did not turn with them but went off by the mill track alone, light and shod for speed, and at the mill a rider in the Second's colours asked after a captain with a stick and a carter with oxen (plant for b2.2; unnamed). Back at the inn the uncle names his price for what comes next: a reader of writs rides in at the noon bell tomorrow to read the list again at Coldmere's bell-house. Rae means to stand the price on her own debt; Darrow refuses to let her pay for him; they have it out in the yard, both with a point, and he leaves the choice with her because it is hers.
slots.turn: Darrow lets someone else decide what she will pay for him, which no man of the Ninth ever saw him do; the bell-house will read his name at noon.

slots.plan: Rae at her uncle's table after the inn has gone to bed (written on the Wednesday or Thursday close): the book of the debt and the load she pays into it; the uncle's question, what the captain of the Ninth is worth to the Holloway; a packet in salt for the river mill that she carries and does not open; the thing she wanted, a thing carried up the mountain and seen come down whole, and what she finds she wants now that she has had it. Thread 18 tells only; nothing named; her father and the cage stay for Tether II.
slots.turn: Rae, who carries and never keeps, admits to herself that she has kept something, and does not put it down.

world_moves: a levy column went south along the Holloway toward the ford villages, driving the farms' cattle ahead of it
a Confessor's rider passed on the Holloway with a satchel of writs for every bell-post below the mountain
sleet closed the drove road for a morning, and the company sheltered under the cart until it passed

climax.plan: The Bell at Coldmere (arc b2.1). At the noon bell a reader of writs, two grey cloaks and the levy read the list at Coldmere's bell-house, where it was first read: the Captain of the Ninth above every other, the Mender Vorne under it, Hollis's name among the Sixth's. The village stands in the road; the uncle stands at his door; Rae's choice from Saturday decides who stands where. By tier (arc b2.1; the levy sergeant already gone unless Costly brings him back): Triumph, the uncle hides them for Rae's sake and sends the readers' men the wrong way, and the village that has heard of the bell turns its back on the writ; Hard-won, a night in a barn on the tarn and away before the dawn bell, Ash giving them away once and forgiven; Costly, the levy sergeant comes back and knows Hollis's name, and they leave Coldmere at a walk with the village watching, Rae's custom on the Holloway spent for him; Setback, the writ is nailed to the inn's door with his epithet on it, and the Lowmarch knows what he is called before he does. Then the road out, and the choice.
checks: insight (Warden's Eye: the reader, the uncle, and who in the crowd will speak)
resolve (the Mender's Patience: standing in the road while his name is read, and not stepping forward this time)
finesse (the cart, the mule and five people out of Coldmere unseen)
options: East by the river road, where the levies are driving the farms in front of them.
North by the mill tracks, the safe road for his own.

quest_summary: Confessor Ivo Marrant is coming up the Holloway with five grey cloaks (six in all), a cart, a censer, and a writ naming the Faithless at Saint Ysolde's. Darrow's name is first; Hollis is second. Rae Thorne, the carter who heard the list read, is in the House; her cart and oxen wait at the winch-house below, where one of the six will stay; the rest camp on the lower terrace under the gate.
